notes: The session's shared web-search allowance (200) ran out about two thirds of the way through; after that, pages were opened directly: each government's own site, the candidates' own sites, Wikipedia's election articles and named news organizations. Campaign addresses came from a voter-guide site's links (used only as leads) or from trying an address; each was kept only when the site's own pages name the candidate and the office or place.

No birth year is recorded for anyone. Wikipedia gives a birth date for John S. Leiber (1977) but no citation was seen beside it, so it is left out; ages printed in WisPolitics interviews (Bill Oemichen, Bernie Newman) fit two birth years each and are left out.

No party's own published endorsement was found for these 30; ballot/lean/wi_endorsements.json already holds the party pages that list Jay Schroeder, John S. Leiber and Bernie Newman in other words. Endorsements shown on candidates' own sites are not party pages and are not recorded.

Left out on purpose: Mike Morgan's only listed campaign page is a social media page; donovanforassembly.com names Bob Donovan and District 61 but its newest item is from August 2024, so it is not recorded as his 2026 site; Tom Hausner's earlier police posts are jobs, not offices, and only the undersheriff post is recorded.

Nothing found under the rules for: Brandon White (the City of Jefferson's municipal court page names no judge), Joel Richmond, Maureen McCarville, Randy Udell, Bernie Newman (a TMJ4 report of his plan commission service could not be reopened), Bob Donovan, Karen Kirsch, Henry Johnson, Mark S. Maier, Bob Look, Jeff Foster. Michele Magadance Skinner's residency lawsuit is a legal matter and is not recorded.
Pages that publish contact details (county supervisor lists, campaign footers) were read for the name, title and term only; no address, phone or e-mail is in this file.

For the verifier: dylanforassembly.com, dowlingforassembly.com and schnitzlerforassembly.com answer the kit's fetcher with 429 and were read with WebFetch; the 2024 runs are in the results table of Wikipedia's article (districts 73, 90, 95).

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every url was reopened (WebFetch, and the kit's fetcher where WebFetch could not find the host). Pages that carry contact details were read for name, title, office and term only.
